How to play

  1. Press Play. Rabbits eat the grass and multiply. Foxes chase the rabbits.
  2. Watch the chart: rabbits boom, then foxes boom, then rabbits crash, then foxes crash. Again and again.
  3. Try the three presets, then the sliders. Turn on Equations mode to compare with the maths.

What's happening?

  • Lots of grass means lots of fed rabbits, so rabbits boom.
  • Lots of rabbits means easy meals, so foxes boom, a little later.
  • Now foxes eat rabbits faster than they're born. Rabbits crash.
  • No rabbits, no food: foxes hit their hunger limit and starve. Foxes crash. The grass grows back, and it starts again.
  • The rabbits-vs-foxes plot turns those waves into a loop. Each trip round is one cycle.
  • Equations mode shows the Lotka-Volterra equations (1920s). They have no grass, no space and no bad luck, so their loop never dies out. Real animals can.

Try this: start from Everything crashes. Can you change just one slider so rabbits and foxes live together for 1,000 days? Which slider did it, and why does it help?
